families.family: wyrm — Godzilla (MonsterVerse evolutionary ladder: gz2014 → burning → gvk → gxk → supernova). One animal escalating; distinctness rides on plate jaggedness/height/count, body bulk/lean, palette + self-illumination, NOT silhouette. All 5 share buildWyrm + drawTorso/drawPlates/drawHead/drawLeg/drawArm/drawTailScaled/drawRidgeElement/drawFissures in js/archetypes.js, data-driven by shape{}/palette in js/config.js lines 108-145.

No selfIllum (correct — matte unlit rock). The ONE concrete spec violation is the eye color.

forms.assessment: Strong: the #1 brand cue (lava fissures) and incandescent plate gradient both fire. config.js:121 fissures:0.5 → drawFissures draws 5 thick opaque branching seams (archetypes.js:96-116, core lineWidth 2.6). plateHot:['#ff5a14','#ffd24a'] (config.js:119) feeds opts.faceGrad so plates bake a hot base→tip gradient (drawPlates:278-282). selfIllum:true + rimGlow:'#ff7a1a' → drawTorso re-strokes the full silhouette orange (archetypes.js:220-232). Charred body #2c2622 is darker than 2014 grey so cracks pop. The gap is the SILHOUETTE escalation: spec says the ridge is 'a notch TALLER and SHARPER … one visibly taller hot lead-plate breaks the skyline,' but the code delivers neither.

For the lead plate, add a small targeted spike in drawPlates: after computing size, if i === Math.round(N*0.55) multiply size *= 1.35 (a deterministic 'hot lead plate' near the shoulder apex) — wyrm-local, only fires when a new opt like opts.leadPlate is set so other forms are untouched.

Blue plateGlow is live FX, not baked. Two issues: (1) the skin is blue-tinted vs the spec's neutral charcoal, risking a premature 'cool' read; (2) gvk has NO plateHeightMul so its taller-than-2014 read leans only on removing 2014's 0.85, which is correct but the razor-narrowing could push harder.

BUT: (1) the body is FAR lighter than the near-black violet the spec mandates, risking the opposite of the night-sky problem (no longer near-black, but also no longer the dramatic 'dark mass lifted by a violet rim'); (2) the crystal 3-stop plate gradient is NOT implemented — plates bake flat; (3) bulk and plate height undershoot the 'biggest + ×1.4 overgrown ridge' silhouette delta that IS supernova's identity.

sharedHelperChanges.change: Currently only supports a 2-stop linear gradient via opts.faceGrad[0]/[1]. To deliver supernova's spec'd 3-stop crystal gradient (#2a1448→#a55ae6→#dcb0ff) faithfully, extend it to detect a length-3 array and addColorStop(0,0.5,1). OPTIONAL — a 2-stop ['#522485','#dcb0ff'] reads nearly the same at 40px and needs no helper edit.
sharedHelperChanges.rationale: Cross-form regression risk: burning ALSO uses faceGrad (plateHot:['#ff5a14','#ffd24a']). If you change the gradient logic, the 2-stop branch must remain the default so burning's plates are byte-identical. Guard the 3-stop with an array-length check, not a rewrite. Lowest-risk path is to add supernova's plateHot as a 2-stop and touch no shared code at all.

sharedHelperChanges.change: burning's 'one taller hot lead-plate' needs a targeted per-index size spike. Add it behind a NEW opt (e.g. opts.leadPlate) so the spike only fires for burning: if (opts.leadPlate && i === Math.round(N*opts.leadPlate)) size *= 1.35;
sharedHelperChanges.rationale: Cross-form regression risk: every wyrm form calls drawPlates. Gating the spike on a new opt that only burning sets (config.js:121) keeps gz2014/gvk/gxk/supernova plate rows untouched. Do NOT bake the spike unconditionally — it would corrupt the deterministic hash() jitter symmetry on the other four forms.

sharedHelperChanges.change: No code change — but note supernova's body-darkening fix relies on the existing light→skin→dark gradient direction (top→bottom). The spec's 'raise the AO BOTTOM to #2a1448 (never pure black)' means skinDark (the bottom stop) must be set LIGHTER than skin for supernova, which is unusual vs the other forms where skinDark is darker.
sharedHelperChanges.rationale: This is a per-form palette inversion, not a helper edit, so no regression risk to other forms — but flag it because a future editor 'fixing' supernova's skinDark to be darker-than-skin (matching the family pattern) would re-break the night-visibility the spec mandates.

families.family: Mothra (flyer family) — buildFlyer + drawMothThorax / drawMothWing / drawFlyerHead / drawAltitudeShadow in js/archetypes.js, data-driven by config.js FORMS shape{}/palette (mothra_gvm L148-154, mothra_gxk L155-161, mothra_supernova L162-168). forms.assessment: Strongest of the three. The four-wing bilateral spread (drawMothWing fore+hind lobes), the concentric eyespot (border #1a1a22 / blue iris #2ec8ff / off-white center), the cream furred oval thorax (drawMothThorax gradient skinLight→skin→skinDark) and the amber/yellow wingField bands all read correctly, and blue is correctly an ACCENT (eyes + eyespot iris) over a white-fur body — the original cyan-glowing-lizard bug is fixed. Two genuine misses keep it from 'indistinguishable': the antennae are drawn in pal.skinDark (= #b8aa92 taupe, near-invisible on the cream head) instead of the spec's WHITE swept-back antennae, and the brown-orange forehead tuft (#8a5a2c) the spec calls a signatureCue has no draw code at all. Neither breaks the species read but both are listed must-haves, and white antennae are cheap silhouette identity.

Either add a shape/palette field eyespotIris (e.g. #ffd700 gold) consumed at L656, or for the supernova form set pal.eye to gold #ffd700 and use pal.skinLight (#ffffff) only for the hot center — yielding dark-gold→gold→white-hot as specced. gaps.cue: Widest, LEVEL, symmetric 'descending angel' wing pose — reduced forward sweep (mustHaveForBlindID, the silhouette escalation over t1/t2)

The WH cap at 50 also means wingSpan 2.7→3.3 barely changes span once capped (BH*3.3*0.125 with BH≈124*1.0 ≈ 51 → capped to 50 anyway), so 'widest spread' under-delivers.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a shape.wingLevel (or reuse godrays) flag: when set, raise the forewing tipY toward body level (e.g. -BH*0.78 instead of -BH*0.92) and reduce the lean-sweep term, so the wings sit flatter/'level' — the descending-angel read. Also raise the WH cap or the bulk for supernova so wingSpan 3.3 actually produces the widest span (currently the 50px cap flattens the t1→t3 span escalation); verify the wider/level tips still clear x∈[0,150].

families.family: King Ghidorah (hydra — three-headed serpentine neck-fan). Forms: ghidorah (MV 2019), king_ghidorah (Heisei 1991), mecha_ghidorah (Mecha-King 1991), grand_king (Grand King 1998), void_ghidorah (AniGoji 2018). Shared draw path: buildHydra → drawHydraHeads → drawHydraNeck + drawGhidorahHead + drawBatWing, on the wyrm drawTorso/drawLeg/drawTail body. All five share ONE neck-fan layout function (drawHydraHeads), ONE head function (drawGhidorahHead, with a headHornStyle branch), and ONE wing function (drawBatWing). The family read 'three necks + two wings' is delivered; the per-tier separators are where it's thin. Biggest cross-form structural issue: the center-forward depth cue (THE MV identifier and a baseline for all five) is only half-delivered — the center neck is taller/larger but is NOT consistently drawn in front (plain n=0..2 loop means the right outer neck overlaps the center). Verified by reading drawHydraHeads lines 1022-1063: no front-center z-reorder.

forms.assessment: Reads as a 3-neck gold dragon with bat-wings and two tails — the family read survives. But the form's headline MV identifier (center neck thrust FORWARD of the outer two, asymmetric trident) is only partially delivered, and the 'soft emotive curved crown' that separates it from Heisei T2 is the SAME prong fan as T2 minus one prong — the curvature/softness the spec demands is not encoded. The biggest practical risk is T1 vs T2 collapse: both are gold 3-head fans drawn by identical code with only neckSpread (1.25 vs 1.45), neckLenMul (1.0 vs 1.15), perSide horn count (3 vs 4) and skin value (#d4a000 vs #f2c200) differing. At 40px those are subtle and the horn shape is byte-identical-shaped (straight raked prongs) for both.

gaps.cue: Center neck/head forward & dominant over the two outer ones (the MV-specific asymmetric trident — a mustHaveForBlindID)
gaps.currentCode: drawHydraHeads (lines 1022-1063) loops n=0,1,2 with no front-center reorder. Center (n=1) gets neckLen bonus +0.10 and headScale*1.12 (tallest+largest, good) but is drawn SECOND, so the right outer neck (n=2) renders ON TOP of it — the center is overlapped, not 'in front'. rootX for center has no forward push along the facing axis; all the spec's 'center pushed FORWARD' depth is absent in X.
gaps.proposedFix: In drawHydraHeads, draw the center head LAST (reorder the loop so centerIdx renders after the outer necks, e.g. iterate outer indices then center, or sort by |frac| descending). Add a forward-along-facing nudge to the center root/tip: tipX += lean * BH * 0.06 and tipY -= BH * 0.04 when isCenter, so the center head sits higher AND overlaps both siblings. This is the single highest-leverage MV cue and also benefits every other tier's center-dominance read.

gaps.cue: Soft emotive CURVED back-swept horn crown (vs Heisei's rigid straight rack) — the T1-vs-T2 silhouette separator
gaps.currentCode: drawGhidorahHead horn loop (lines 947-956): perSide=3, prongLean = -0.5 - p*0.12, drawn with drawRidgeElement which makes STRAIGHT triangular prongs (apex = x+lean*size, a straight line). There is no curvature; T1 and T2 use the identical straight-prong primitive, differing only in count (3 vs 4) and length. The 'curved/soft' MV crown is not represented at all.
gaps.proposedFix: Give 'crown' (T1) a distinct curved profile vs 'crown_tall' (T2). Cheapest: reduce T1 prongLean magnitude and ADD a per-prong lean increment that fans them into an arc (e.g. prongLean = -0.35 - p*0.20 with a small +outward x-drift) so they read as a soft swept fan, while T2 keeps steep uniform near-vertical leans for a rigid rack. Or add a curve flag to drawRidgeElement that bends the apex. Pair with widthMul: pass a wider widthMul (~0.6) for T1's blunt-soft crown vs a narrow razor widthMul (~0.32) for T2's spiky rack.

gaps.cue: Bat-wing SCALLOPED trailing edge (finger-spar membrane, distinct from Rodan's single-point wing)
gaps.currentCode: drawBatWing (lines 991-995) draws a concave quadraticCurveTo per spar gap with control offset (-side*BH*0.05, +BH*0.04). The scallop depth (BH*0.05) is shallow and at 40px reads as a soft wobble, not crisp bat-notches.
gaps.proposedFix: Deepen the scallop control offset to ~BH*0.08-0.09 and make the notches HARD (the spec's hardAt40px: 'cut them as hard concave notches'), e.g. pull each mid control point further inboard so each gap reads as a distinct V. This is a shared-helper edit — see sharedHelperChanges (affects all four winged tiers, not void).

gaps.cue: Sickle tail-barbs at each tail tip
gaps.currentCode: buildHydra uses the wyrm drawTail (lines 156-165) for both tails — a smooth tapering quad with NO barb. The spec's 'forked-sickle / spiky SICKLE barb' is absent on all hydra tiers.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a small filled barb triangle at the tail tip in drawTail when called from hydra (pass an opts.barb flag, or add a hydra-specific drawHydraTail). A 3-vertex hook at (d*BW*1.25, -BH*0.06) costs nothing and adds the family tail signature.

priorityFixes: Make the center head render LAST + nudge it forward-along-facing (drawHydraHeads) so the MV asymmetric-trident / center-dominance cue actually reads — fixes the #1 mustHaveForBlindID and helps all five tiers.
Differentiate T1 soft-curved crown from T2 rigid-straight rack (drawGhidorahHead horn loop + widthMul) so T1/T2 don't collapse into 'two gold fans'.
Deepen the wing scallops into hard notches so 'bat-wing' survives at 40px (shared drawBatWing).

forms.assessment: This is the most at-risk form: its entire identity is 'visibly brighter/taller/wider + STRAIGHT rigid devil-horns vs MV'. The size/spread deltas ARE encoded (neckSpread 1.45, neckLenMul 1.15, wingSpan 2.9, headHornStyle 'crown_tall' = 4 prongs +30% len +1 hooked tip). But the load-bearing STRAIGHT-vs-CURVED horn distinction does not exist in code: both T1 and T2 draw the SAME straight raked drawRidgeElement prongs — so the only thing separating them at 40px is a count (3 vs 4) and a ~one-step gold value bump (#d4a000 → #f2c200). The spec explicitly warns 'if T1 and T2 share gold value they collapse'; #d4a000 vs #f2c200 is a real but modest luminance step, and with identical horn shape the two tiers are easy to confuse.

gaps.cue: RIGID STRAIGHT devil-horn rack (the Heisei silhouette signature; spec: 'denser, longer, more vertical/rigid prong fan, 4-per-side, +30% length, one hooked tall crown tip')
gaps.currentCode: drawGhidorahHead (lines 945-956): style 'crown_tall' sets perSide=4 and plen*1.3 (length+30% ✓) and the last prong gets +0.55 length (hooked crown tip ✓ length, but it's not actually hooked — just longer). BUT prongLean = -0.5 - p*0.12 is the SAME swept lean as T1's 'crown' — so the rack is raked-back identical to MV, not vertical/rigid. There is no straightness/verticality differentiator.
gaps.proposedFix: For 'crown_tall', override prongLean toward near-vertical and uniform (e.g. prongLean = -0.20 fixed, low magnitude) so the prongs stand straight up as a rigid devil rack, contrasting T1's swept fan. Narrow the prong width (pass widthMul ~0.30 to drawRidgeElement) so they read as sharp spikes. Make the hooked tip an actual hook: for the last prong, draw a short reverse-lean cap segment.

gaps.cue: Visibly brighter METALLIC gold value step vs MV (the primary differentiator per spec)
gaps.currentCode: palette skin #f2c200 vs T1 #d4a000, skinLight #fff0a0 vs #f0d070. The value step exists but is modest; the 'metallic specular crest' the spec calls for (rgba(255,250,235,0.22) near-white specular) is only the shared house rimCol(0.30/0.45) on the neck crest — identical strength to T1's rim. No brighter specular crest is applied to distinguish T2.
gaps.proposedFix: Bump T2's neck crestRim alpha higher than T1 (pass rimCol(0.55) for T2 vs 0.30 for T1) for a brighter metallic specular crest, and/or push skin lighter (#f7cc1a) so the luminance gap from #d4a000 clears the 40px wash threshold the spec flags.

gaps.cue: Pronounced HOOKED wing-tips on fin-like bat-wings (Heisei wing signature)
gaps.currentCode: drawBatWing is shape-identical for T1 and T2 (same spars=4, same scallop math). No hooked wing-tip is cut for T2; there's no opts hook for it.
gaps.proposedFix: Add an opts.wingHook flag passed only for king_ghidorah; in drawBatWing extend the outermost spar tip (tipsX/Y[spars]) into a small recurved hook (extra lineTo that doubles back), cut as a notch per the spec's hardAt40px. Keeps T1's wing un-hooked for contrast.

priorityFixes: Make 'crown_tall' an actually STRAIGHT/rigid near-vertical narrow rack (override prongLean + widthMul in drawGhidorahHead) — without this T2 is just T1+1prong and the tiers collapse.
Widen the gold luminance gap from T1: brighter skin + brighter specular crestRim alpha so the 'metallic step up' survives at 40px.
Cut hooked wing-tips for T2 only (drawBatWing opts) to add a second silhouette separator from T1.

forms.assessment: Strongest-delivered of the five: the cyborg-center read is genuinely encoded — center neck uses drawMechHead (angular helmet skull + cyan visor bar + panel seam + steel neck-brace bands) while the two outer necks switch to a gold sub-palette (goldSkin #e6b800 etc.) via drawGhidorahHead. The gold-organic-sides vs silver-machine-center contrast (the whole identity) reads. Remaining risks: (1) the torso steel overlay is drawn at low effective alpha (drawMechPanels called at 0.55, then internally *0.65 = ~0.36) so the body reads as a translucent grey wash over gold rather than 'hard silver plating at full opacity' the spec demands; (2) the center skull is angular but not dramatically BLOCKIER in silhouette than the rounded gold heads, so the 'rounded-square-rounded' fan read the spec wants is weak; (3) the wings use opts.mech (flat panel + cyan edge) which is good, but the membrane is filled with pal.skin (#808080) at full — fine.

gaps.cue: Hard SILVER plating on chest/torso at FULL opacity with seams (spec: 'not a translucent wash')
gaps.currentCode: buildHydra line 855 calls drawMechPanels(...,0.55); drawMechPanels line 1212 then does globalAlpha = alpha*0.65 → ~0.357 effective fill alpha on the chest/shoulder/belly panels. At 40px over a gold torso this reads as a grey haze, not opaque steel — directly the failure the spec warns against.
gaps.proposedFix: Raise the torso panel opacity for mecha_ghidorah: pass alpha ~0.92 from buildHydra (the comment says 'partial for gold-steel mix' but the spec wants the torso/chest fully machine; only the OUTER NECKS stay gold). Or special-case: keep panels opaque (alpha 1.0 * 0.9) and let the gold show only on the two outer necks, which already happens. This makes the silver/gold split crisp.

gaps.cue: Center head a distinctly BLOCKY/angular silhouette so the fan reads 'rounded-square-rounded' before color resolves (spec hardAt40px #1)
gaps.currentCode: drawHydraHeads line 1059 draws the center via drawMechHead with headStyle 'helmet' — an angular wedge (lines 1425-1431), which is more angular than the gold ellipse heads, but it's a soft wedge, not a hard box. The outer gold heads are drawGhidorahHead ellipses. The blocky-vs-round contrast exists but is mild.
gaps.proposedFix: For the cyborg center, force a hard rectangular box skull (headStyle 'box' path, lines 1432-1434, draws ctx.rect) instead of 'helmet', or widen the helmet wedge so the center reads as a clear square block. The squarer the center vs the round sides, the better the fan reads at 40px.

gaps.cue: Cyan visor slit as a bright horizontal bar that pops against the silver skull
gaps.currentCode: drawMechHead 'helmet' branch (lines 1459-1464) draws a plate-colored backing rect then a cyan (pal.eye = #00d6ff) rect at globalAlpha 0.90 — a visor bar exists ✓. But it's drawn at 0.90 alpha and sized hw*0.74 — at the center head's small scale (BH*0.60*headScale) it may thin out.
gaps.proposedFix: Bump the visor cyan to full opacity and ensure min height (Math.max(2, ...)) so the cyan bar survives at iso; this is the cheapest machine-center tell. Minor because it mostly already works.

priorityFixes: Raise the torso steel-panel opacity (buildHydra alpha 0.55 → ~0.9) so the silver plating reads as hard armor, not a grey wash — the spec's explicit must-have.
Make the cyborg center skull a harder BLOCK (headStyle 'box' or a squarer helmet) so the 'rounded-square-rounded' fan reads at 40px.
Guarantee the cyan visor bar survives at the center head's small scale (full alpha + min height).

forms.assessment: At-risk: the #1 Grand King identifier is the horn ASYMMETRY (FORKED branching center crown + STRAIGHT side crowns). The code attempts this (headHornStyle 'asymmetric' branch in drawGhidorahHead lines 953-955 adds an extra forked sub-prong on the center head only), but the fork is a single small offset prong, not a clear Y/antler mass — at 40px it reads as one slightly-bushier center crown, not 'forked center vs straight sides'. The bulk cue is under-delivered: bodyBulk 1.12 (spec wants ~1.18) and neckLenMul 0.92 (shorter necks ✓) but neck WIDTH is not thickened (spec wants neck base ~BH*0.135 stocky; code uses the default BH*0.11 base). So 'beefier, shorter, THICKER necks' is only half there. Palette is the brightest gold (#ffee77 ✓) which is good, but with weak fork + thin necks it can collapse toward the other gold tiers.

gaps.cue: FORKED/branching antler on CENTER head reading as a Y/antler mass (the load-bearing separator) vs STRAIGHT side horns
gaps.currentCode: drawGhidorahHead lines 953-955: for 'asymmetric'+isCenter, adds ONE extra drawRidgeElement per prong at offset (px - len2*0.16, py - len2*0.4), len2*0.6 — a thin secondary prong. This makes the center crown denser but not a clear FORK; the side heads run the same base loop (3 straight prongs) so 'center forked vs sides straight' is barely distinguishable at iso. Spec hardAt40px: 'build the forked center crown as a Y-shaped FILLED triangular mass (two sub-prongs sharing a base).'
gaps.proposedFix: Rebuild the center fork as a true Y: for each center prong draw TWO sub-prongs sharing the base (split near the tip into a V), as a filled mass — e.g. one drawRidgeElement leaning -prongLean+0.3 and one leaning -prongLean-0.3 from the same base point, both shorter, forming a fork. Keep the SIDE heads at single straight prongs (they already are). The contrast in crown silhouette is the whole ID.

gaps.cue: Shorter + THICKER (stocky) necks vs the lean gold tiers
gaps.currentCode: neckLenMul 0.92 in config (shorter ✓). But nwBase in drawHydraHeads (line 1037) = BH*0.11*widthMul with widthMul=1 (grand_king sets no neckWidthMul) — SAME base width as T1. Spec hardAt40px: 'exaggerate neck base width (~BH*0.135)'. So necks are shorter but not thicker → reads lean-but-short, not stocky.
gaps.proposedFix: Add neckWidthMul ~1.25 to grand_king's shape{} (drawHydraHeads already multiplies nwBase/nwTip by widthMul, line 1037-1038), giving ~BH*0.137 base — the stocky read. Also bump bodyBulk 1.12 → 1.18 per spec so the heavier outline carries the bulk delta.

gaps.cue: Beefiest/bulkiest body of the organic tiers
gaps.currentCode: bodyBulk 1.12 (config line 197) feeds BH = h*0.74*0.74*bodyBulk. Spec wants ~1.18. Modest under-delivery; combined with thin necks the bulk doesn't read.
gaps.proposedFix: bodyBulk 1.12 → 1.18 (verify the taller neck-fan still clears the canvas top at this bulk; reduce neckLenMul slightly if it clips, which aligns with the stocky-neck goal anyway).

priorityFixes: Rebuild the center crown as a TRUE filled Y-fork (two sub-prongs per prong sharing a base) while keeping side heads straight — the canonical asymmetry and the only thing that separates Grand King from the other gold tiers.
Add neckWidthMul ~1.25 so the necks read STOCKY (shorter+thicker), not just shorter.
Push bodyBulk to ~1.18 for the beefier silhouette (verify canvas-top bounds).

forms.assessment: Mostly well-delivered and the most differentiated tier. The thorns (drawHydraNeck opts.thorns, lines 897-910), cyan crest rim (neckRim rgba(0,224,255,0.7)), gold mid-vein, static S-bend (sBend via hash, line 1029), thin long necks (neckLenMul 1.25, neckWidthMul 0.65), and the wormhole portal (buildHydra voidPortal branch, lines 808-815) are all present — this reads as the alien thorny-neck-from-a-portal entity the spec wants, and the cyan rim lifts the near-black indigo body off the night sky. The main fidelity gap is a CONTRADICTION with the spec's silhouette: the spec says Void has NO wings, NO solid body, NO tails ('the form that breaks the dragon mold') — but buildHydra ALWAYS draws bat-wings, a torso, legs, and two tails for every hydra form including void. So void currently renders as a winged, legged, two-tailed dragon with thorny necks, which the spec explicitly calls a failure ('if it grows wings or a normal torso it reads as dark Ghidorah and fails').

gaps.cue: NO wings, NO solid body, NO legs, NO tails — just thorny necks emerging from a portal (mustHaveForBlindID + commonMisreads failure mode)
gaps.currentCode: buildHydra unconditionally draws: tails (lines 826-832), bat wings (836 & 859), legs (840-842), torso (845). There is no voidPortal/bodyless branch — void_ghidorah gets the full winged dragon body plus its thorny necks. This directly contradicts the spec's core silhouette and its named failure mode.
gaps.proposedFix: Gate the body parts on a 'bodyless' flag (s.voidPortal): when set, SKIP wings, legs, torso, and tails, and instead anchor the three thorny necks directly to the wormhole disc origin (root the necks at the portal center pcy = -BH*0.28 rather than -BH*0.82). This is the largest single fidelity win for void and the only way it stops reading as 'dark winged Ghidorah'. Cross-check the portal disc size/position so the neck roots emerge from it.

gaps.cue: Thorns surviving as silhouette bumps + tips catching the cyan rim
gaps.currentCode: drawHydraNeck thorns (lines 897-910): drawn for k=2..N-1 (~5 thorns/neck), length m[4]*1.7 (~1.7x half-width), filled in thornCol = np.skinLight (#5a5a82) — a DARK indigo-grey, so the thorns blend into the dark neck rather than catching the cyan rim. Spec: 'thorn tips catch the cyan rim.'
gaps.proposedFix: Stroke the thorn tips with the cyan crestRim (rgba(0,224,255,...)) so they read as bright spikes against the dark neck, per spec. Optionally increase thorn length slightly (m[4]*2.0) so the larger ones survive as silhouette bumps at 40px.

gaps.cue: Necks as the dominant mass (longest/thinnest, writhing) — should fill the silhouette since there's no body
gaps.currentCode: neckLenMul 1.25 + neckWidthMul 0.65 give long thin necks ✓, but because the (to-be-removed) torso/wings still occupy the lower silhouette, the necks currently look like normal-length dragon necks on a body. Once the body is gated off (above), the necks should be lengthened/re-rooted from the portal to dominate.
gaps.proposedFix: After gating the body, re-root necks at the portal (rootY ≈ portal center) and consider neckLenMul ~1.4 so they dominate the frame as the spec's 'longest of all tiers'. Verify tips stay within the 150x168 canvas.

priorityFixes: Gate OFF wings/legs/torso/tails for void_ghidorah (s.voidPortal) and root the thorny necks at the wormhole — without this it reads as a dark winged Ghidorah, the spec's explicit failure mode.
Cyan-tip the thorns (stroke tips in neckRim) so the rose-thorn signature pops against the dark indigo necks.
After de-bodying, lengthen/re-root the necks from the portal so they dominate the silhouette as the alien writhing-stem read.

sharedHelperChanges.helper: drawHydraHeads (lines 1009-1065) — shared by ALL five forms
sharedHelperChanges.change: Reorder so the CENTER head renders LAST (after both outer necks) and add a forward-along-facing nudge for the center (tipX += lean*BH*0.06, tipY -= BH*0.04 when isCenter). Currently a plain n=0..2 loop overlaps the center with the right outer neck.

CROSS-FORM REGRESSION RISK: changing draw order affects every tier's neck overlap — verify Heisei/Grand King (which are meant to be MORE symmetric than MV) don't now look TOO center-dominant; the forward nudge can be MV-only (gate on a shape flag like centerForward:true) so Heisei stays symmetric. Re-render all 5 + multiple facings (base 0/2/4) to check no neck clips the canvas or detaches from the torso.

Today 'crown' and 'crown_tall' use the SAME prongLean swept formula and the same default width.

CROSS-FORM REGRESSION RISK: this function draws every head on every tier including the outer gold heads of mecha_ghidorah; ensure the 'crown' branch (used by both ghidorah AND mecha's outer heads) stays consistent — mecha's outer gold heads should keep T1's crown, which is fine if the branch is keyed on headHornStyle.
